goal: Ship the SolicitationReleasePoller: the one Postgres-state-driven loop that releases approved Outreach rows through the fixed governor order, writes the two system Halt latch reasons, terminalizes wedged sending rows as unknown, and backstops the join via closeBatchIfSettled.
non_goals: No migration. Migration 091 and 110 already carry every column, CHECK member and partial unique index this feature writes.
No auto-approval lane, no 60-minute confirmed-delivery veto anchor, no auto_approval_policies widening (#631).
No review_attributed writer (#632) - the outcome kind stays writer-less here.
No staging flag flip and no flag evidence (#633).
No resume and no un-halt. The Halt latch is monotone and the release predicate requires halted_at IS NULL.

No platform_halt halt reason and no halt-aware send window. Amendment B14 assigns that gap to #900, but both fixes need a 091 CHECK widening and this ticket ships no migration. Deferred to a new follow-up issue; B14's accepted first horn stands.
No owner notification when a Judge outage downgrades an approved batch. A spine step plus a Sentry warning is the whole record.

No genuine priority-yielding against the shared Resend 10 req/s team limit. The per-tick release budget is the scheduling lever the releaser owns; true yielding needs a shared limiter view and is not built.
user_visible_behavior: An approved Solicitation batch past its veto deadline starts dripping: Outreach rows move rendered to queued and one solicitation_send job is enqueued per row.
Release stops at the account daily send cap (LEAST(configured, 10)) and at the platform daily ceiling, so a 25-ask batch is forced across at least three calendar days.
Release stops entirely while the Send breaker is open, while SOLICITATION_SEND_ENABLED is off, and while the account's subscription does not grant full access.
A batch whose 72h send window elapses is halted with reason send_window_elapsed, its live Outreach rows are cancelled, and its Send batch parent terminalizes cancelled.
A batch that receives no approval within the 7-day approval window is halted with reason batch_expired and closes the same way, so it never reaches the 11-day stalled threshold.
An Outreach row wedged in sending with no in-flight outbox row past 60 minutes terminalizes unknown and raises a Sentry alert, freeing the location's one-active-send slot.

A Judge outage before the first release returns the batch to owner review: approved_at, approval_method and approved_by_user_id are cleared and the batch reappears as approvable in the Requests panel.
A Judge outage mid-drip holds the batch with no state change; releases resume on recovery, or the 72h window expires and the batch terminalizes cancelled.
invariants: Invariant #2 - transactional outbox: the rendered-to-queued CAS and the solicitation_send job_outbox INSERT commit in ONE transaction.
Invariant #2 - the job_outbox in-flight status set ('pending', 'dispatching', 'dispatched') is re-spelled by hand, members and order, per src/lib/shared/job-outbox-status.ts.
Invariant #2 - solicitation_send has a typed helper from this PR onward, so no raw INSERT for that topic may remain (ci:outbox-seam).
The send topic gets BOTH guards: the outreach-row CAS and migration 091's job_outbox_solicitation_send_inflight partial unique index, byte-for-byte with the helper's ON CONFLICT.
Invariant #8 - every read and write is scoped by account_id and business_id. countPlatformDispatchAttemptsToday is the one allowlisted cross-account read.
Invariant #11 - entitlement is gated on subscriptionGrantsFullAccess, never a raw equality against 'active'.
Invariant #15 - src/lib/solicitation/release.ts receives its DB client as an explicit parameter; only the poller (a composition root registered in worker/index.ts) imports the singleton.
The governor order is fixed and load-bearing: Send breaker, then platform ceiling, then account cap, then the per-child Dispatch gate inside #899.
readSendBreaker fails CLOSED. It returns state or throws, and the throw IS the halt signal. No try/catch may wrap it and proceed.
The releaser is a PURE READER of the Send breaker. HealthAlertPoller is its only tripper.
The Halt latch is monotone: a second halt on an already halted batch writes nothing.
The Halt latch never cancels a sending row. Halt means no further sends, not undo.
Halt never terminalizes the Send batch parent directly. closeBatchIfSettled is the single owner of parent terminalization.
Lock order is batch then run, never run then batch. Nothing takes the agent_runs lock for the send parent before calling closeBatchIfSettled.
A row already sending is never re-gated and never re-sent. The unknown sweep is the only writer that may terminalize it.
Caps are enforced in the releaser ONLY. The single-replica worker serializes them by construction; if the releaser is ever parallelized this resolution must be revisited.
edge_cases: A duplicate release attempt for the same Outreach row inserts no second outbox row - the partial unique index makes the helper return null.

SOLICITATION_SEND_ENABLED is flipped OFF mid-drip: the release phase stops, but the three sweeps and the backstop keep running, so the 72h window reclaims the batch instead of wedging the location forever.
The Send breaker is open for days: expiry keeps running under it, so every batch approved in the preceding 72 hours terminalizes cancelled with send_window_elapsed. Accepted per B14; not suppressed.
The account's subscription lapses mid-drip: remaining rows stay rendered, and paying inside the window resumes the drip with no intervention.
A batch with no Send batch parent: latchSystemHalt skips the spine step and still calls closeBatchIfSettled, which returns no_send_parent for an ordinary unapproved batch.
The batch_expired sweep selects only batches that HAVE a Send batch parent, so a watch-mode batch is never latched.
A sending row whose outbox row is still in-flight (pending, dispatching or dispatched) is NOT swept, even past the grace period - the watchdog's re-pend is a normal recovery.
An unknown row counts as possibly contacted for the restraint policy's over_contacted check, but not as a confirmed send for metrics or review_attributed.
A Judge downgrade is only legal before the first release. Migration 091's send-ordering CHECK enforces it: sending_started_at IS NULL OR approved_at IS NOT NULL.
A tick that hits the per-tick release budget leaves the remaining due rows for the next tick; no row is skipped permanently.
The account daily cap counts queued_at within the UTC day, not sent_at - a bounce still spent reputation.
The UTC-day expression keeps its trailing AT TIME ZONE 'UTC'; without it the day silently becomes the session's local day.
A concurrent owner halt during a release tick: the batch row lock serializes them, and the release predicate re-reads halted_at inside the transaction.

rollback_plan: No migration, so rollback is a plain revert of the PR. The feature is inert in production until SOLICITATION_SEND_ENABLED is flipped on, which issue #915 forbids until this ticket lands. Ordered back-out: (1) revert the PR on main and redeploy the Railway worker - the poller is no longer registered and every sweep stops; (2) if a revert is not wanted, set SOLICITATION_RELEASE_POLL_INTERVAL_MS to a large value is NOT a kill switch - use the flag instead: SOLICITATION_SEND_ENABLED=false stops all releases while leaving the sweeps to reclaim in-flight batches after 72h, which is the intended safe state; (3) no data back-out is needed - every write this feature makes is a forward lifecycle transition that closeBatchIfSettled already terminalizes.
observability: One JSON log line per tick from createWorkerLogger('[SolicitationReleasePoller]') carrying released count, per-gate withhold counts, and the three sweep counts. A tick that releases nothing states WHICH gate stopped it.
A Sentry alert on every unknown terminalization - D12d requires it, and the alert is the only signal that a send may have reached a customer unattributably.
A Sentry warning when a Judge outage downgrades an approved batch, because the owner is not notified.
A structured warn line when the per-tick release budget is hit, so the ramp can tell 'paced' from 'capped'.
checkOldestPendingOutbox and checkFailedOutboxByTopic already work on the solicitation_send topic unmodified, because Shape B keeps every in-flight send row due-now. No alerting change is needed.

How I would know it broke: batches sitting in the approved Batch state with a due veto deadline and zero queued rows, or solicitation_send_batch_stalled firing at 11 days, which the batch_expired sweep is supposed to make unreachable.
